title: Drain-safe VCF Operations credential rotation
prompt:
The `vcf-ops-credential-rotation` repo holds the runbook tooling we use to rotate the vCenter collection service account in VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1. `Invoke-VcfOpsCredentialRotation` in `src/VcfOpsCredentialRotation/VcfOpsCredentialRotation.psm1` is still a stub. Implement it.

The rotation must not strand collections that are already in flight against the old secret. Overwriting the credential's `fields` in place cuts every adapter instance over at once and kills any cycle already running. Instead: stage a replacement credential, move each bound adapter instance onto it, confirm nothing still references the original, and only then mark the original retired. A collector that is busy mid-cycle rejects a repoint with a 503 — that is retryable, and an adapter left behind on the old credential means the original must not be retired.

Constraints:

- Use only the eight operations named in `docs/contract.json`, which is derived from the VCF Operations OpenAPI specification. Any other endpoint is refused.
- Drive all API traffic through the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` cmdlets that are already installed on this machine. Do not hand-roll HTTP and do not vendor the SDK.
- Optional fields you are not setting must be omitted from request bodies, never sent as `null` or `""`.

`README.md` has the full behavioural spec, the request-shape rules, and the exact return shape.

Check your work with:

    pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Verify-Rotation.ps1

It runs offline against a loopback mock of the appliance. Leave `tests/`, `tools/` and `docs/` as they are.

prerequisites.name: VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops
prerequisites.note: Installed by the environment, never vendored by this task.

setup: pwsh -NoProfile -Command "Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Install-Module -Name VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops -RequiredVersion 13.5.0.25380678 -Repository PSGallery -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AllowClobber"

network.note: Setup pulls the SDK from the PowerShell Gallery. Verification is fully offline and contacts no VMware endpoint.

scenario: Three adapter instances bound to the original credential are moved to a staged replacement, including one collector that returns 503 twice before accepting the third default attempt, while an unrelated adapter remains untouched and the original credential is renamed only after a drain check.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves SDK-only traffic, exact omission of unset request members, bounded retry of the busy adapter, complete cutover, a post-cutover drain check, and retirement only after the original credential is unused.
